requirements.statement: Open with a Summary section: one paragraph on who, what, where, and the decision.
Then a Facts section. Every fact cites the document in the file it comes from, in square brackets: [notice of loss], [police report], [invoice 1].

source: (text, request, material) => { const names = material.map(m => m.name.toLowerCase().replace(/\.[^.]+$/,'').replace(/[-_]/g,' ').trim()); const sec = text.split(/^## /m).find(s => /^Facts/i.test(s)) || ''; const sentences = sec.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).filter(s => /\w/.test(s) && !/^Facts/i.test(s)); const bad = []; let at = text.indexOf(sec); for (const s of sentences) { const cites = [...s.matchAll(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g)].map(m => m[1].toLowerCase().trim()); const ok = cites.length && cites.every(c => names.some(n => n === c || n.startsWith(c) || c.startsWith(n))); if (!ok) { const st = text.indexOf(s, at); bad.push({ start: Math.max(st,0), end: Math.max(st,0)+s.length, why: 'fact sentence without a cited document in the file' }); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' fact sentence(s) lack a cited file document' : 'every fact cites a file document', spans: bad }; }
means: Each sentence in the Facts section carries a bracketed citation that names a document in the material.

requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/## Coverage analysis\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n## |$)/i); if (!m) return { ok: false, detail: 'no Coverage analysis section', spans: [] }; const body = m[1]; const hasClause = /clause\s+\d+(\.\d+)?|\b\d+\.\d+\b/i.test(body) && /\[policy\]/i.test(body); const exc = [...body.matchAll(/exclusion\s+\d+(\.\d+)?/gi)]; const uncited = exc.filter(e => { const after = body.slice(e.index, e.index + 250); return !/\[[^\]]+\]/.test(after); }); const ok = hasClause && uncited.length === 0; const start = text.indexOf(m[1]); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'clause cited and exclusions cited' : (!hasClause ? 'no policy clause cited' : uncited.length + ' exclusion(s) without citation'), spans: uncited.map(e => ({ start: start + e.index, end: start + e.index + e[0].length, why: 'exclusion without citation' })) }; }
means: The Coverage analysis section cites a policy clause and every exclusion it names is cited to the policy.

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.

source: if (!m) return { ok: false, detail: 'no Decision section', spans: [] };
return { ok, detail: ok ? 'decision states outcome and clause' : 'decision lacks outcome or clause', spans: [] };
means: The Decision section states covered or not covered and names a clause.

requirements.statement: Never speculate about the insured's intent or honesty.
Take every date, name and figure from the file: add none of your own.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
